title: Invocation-Level Reliability of Tool-Using Agents
abstract: arXiv:2608.26189v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Tool-using agents fail two ways: choosing the wrong tool, or forming wrong arguments, and an early failure of either kind can silently corrupt everything downstream. We measure a correct-invocation rate that separates the two, under both a clean teacher-forced context and the model's own free-running context, on five open-weight models over contamination-free multi-step tasks (depths 1-8). By depth 6, roughly 70% of a model's own clean-context capability is lost to its own earlier mistakes (L6 = 0.686, 0.684). Our central finding concerns the measurement itself. Under exact-match scoring against a fixed gold trajectory, a propagation model's severity and recovery parameters are not merely hard to estimate - they are fixed by the scoring rule. translated_title: 工具使用智能体的调用级可靠性研究
translated_abstract: 工具使用智能体以两种方式失败：选择错误的工具，或形成错误的参数，而这两种失败中的任何一种早期发生都可能无声地破坏下游的一切。我们在两种情境下测量了区分这两种失败的“正确调用率”：一种是干净的教师强制上下文，另一种是模型自身的自由运行上下文，涵盖五个开放权重模型，在无污染的多步任务（深度1-8）上进行。到深度6时，模型自身干净上下文能力的大约70%被其早期错误所损失（L6 = 0.686, 0.684）。我们的核心发现涉及测量本身。在针对固定金标准轨迹的精确匹配评分下，传播模型的严重性和恢复参数不仅难以估计——它们被评分规则固定了。严重性被迫达到其边界（869个被污染步骤中0个正确）；恢复在结构上不可观测（580个被污染步骤中0个回到正轨，而随机预期为0.0058）。这两者都导致了失败。
tldr: 本文发现工具使用智能体的调用级可靠性测量受评分规则结构性限制，严重性和恢复参数无法准确估计，且模型自身错误会显著降低深层任务的性能。
en_tdlr: This paper reveals that invocation-level reliability measurement of tool-using agents is structurally constrained by scoring rules, making severity and recovery parameters unestimable, while self-generated errors significantly degrade performance on deep tasks.
